candidates.evidence: Three bands at ~1347 (D), ~1581 (G) and ~2681 cm-1 (2D) with no other sample modes. I2D/IG ≈ 3.1 by fitted amplitude, which fits mono- or turbostratic few-layer graphene. D/G ≈ 1, so there are significant defects or edges.

candidates.material: nanocrystalline / disordered sp2 carbon (graphitic carbon, amorphous-to-nanocrystalline)
candidates.evidence: D and G are present, but a strong, single, narrow 2D band (FWHM ~40, I2D > IG) argues against purely amorphous carbon.
Same band set. The 2D band is a single Lorentzian rather than the multi-component graphite profile, so this is less likely.

hint_reasoning: No material hint was given. The Au substrate note (solidified droplet or wire after CVD growth) fits a carbon/graphene CVD product.

peaks.assignment: D band (defect-activated, A1g-like breathing mode near K, double resonance)
peaks.source: Lorentzian fit of the spectrum (centre and FWHM, amplitude ~107 above local baseline). Assignment: Ferrari & Basko, Nat. Nanotechnol. 8, 235 (2013); Ferrari et al., PRL 97, 187401 (2006).

peaks.assignment: G band (in-plane C-C stretch, sp2 carbon)
peaks.source: Lorentzian fit (amplitude ~109). Assignment: Ferrari et al., PRL 97, 187401 (2006). Polarization not measured, so no pattern is given.
Lorentzian fit (amplitude ~340). Assignment: Ferrari et al., PRL 97, 187401 (2006); Malard et al., Phys. Rep. 473, 51 (2009).

properties.name: layer number
properties.value: Probably monolayer or electronically decoupled (turbostratic) few-layer. I2D/IG ≈ 3 (amplitude) and the 2D band is a single peak with FWHM ~40 cm-1. A single peak is the expected monolayer shape. The width is larger than for clean exfoliated monolayer (~25-30), consistent with defects or inhomogeneity.
properties.source: Ferrari et al., PRL 97, 187401 (2006); Malard et al., Phys. Rep. 473, 51 (2009)

properties.name: defect level
properties.value: I_D/I_G ≈ 1.0 by amplitude. This is a substantial defect or edge density (nanocrystallite size of order 10-20 nm if the laser is ~532 nm). No resolved D' (~1620) or D+D' (~2940) bands, so the defects are not clearly of the vacancy type.
properties.source: Cançado et al., Appl. Phys. Lett. 88, 163106 (2006); Eckmann et al., Nano Lett. 12, 3925 (2012)

properties.name: excitation wavelength
properties.value: ~532 nm (not stated). D at ~1347 and 2D at ~2681 are consistent with visible excitation near 532 nm, since D and 2D disperse with laser energy.
properties.source: Dispersion of D and 2D with excitation energy, Ferrari & Basko 2013

properties.name: doping/strain
properties.value: G at 1581 cm-1 is slightly above the undoped value (~1580), so there is weak p-doping or compressive strain at most. Au charge transfer and strain cannot be separated without the G–2D correlation analysis, which the data are not good enough for.

artifacts.type: Rayleigh/elastic-line tail near 0 cm-1 (strong rise below ~150 cm-1, peak ~4950 counts) and a weak feature near 26 cm-1 that is probably part of the tail or a filter edge

Broad, slowly varying background (~1000 counts at 200-600, rising to ~1450-1600 counts at 2000-3000). This is probably fluorescence or the Au substrate's luminescence/continuum, and it was treated as a baseline.

citations: Ferrari et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 97, 187401 (2006)
Cançado et al., Appl. Phys. Lett. 88, 163106 (2006)
limits: Laser wavelength and polarization are not given and only a single spectrum was measured. Dispersion-based and polarization-based checks are therefore not possible, and the excitation energy was inferred.
The layer count is not definitive. I2D/IG and the 2D width are affected by defects, doping and the Au substrate, so mono-, turbostratic few-layer and thin graphite are not strictly separable.
The 2D width (~40 cm-1) and the large D intensity mean the film is defective or inhomogeneous. A different spot could give a different D/G ratio.
Au gives no first-order Raman lines, so no substrate peak is reported. The background is probably Au luminescence or fluorescence.
The Au substrate may cause SERS-like enhancement and charge transfer, so absolute intensities and the doping and strain split cannot be trusted.
The spectrum has no information on edge versus point-defect type. D' and D+D' are not resolved above the noise (~±30 counts) around 1620 and 2940 cm-1.
Peak parameters come from simple single-Lorentzian fits on a local constant baseline, with no uncertainties reported.
